note: A beginner voice week at 15 minutes a day with no instrument needed: bare drills stay at 3 minutes, the longer singing is tunes chosen by pick and chord notes over chords the app plays, Do Mi Sol returns every day in a new form, and an ear game sits between singing blocks. Each step says what to press and where to look; the long note is held for as long as feels easy, and its clicks are counted only on day 1 and day 7, to compare.

plan.title: Week 1: Do Mi Sol, in tune
plan.summary: Sing in tune over a drone, skip through Do Mi Sol, and use it in tunes and over chords.

exercises.title: A long Do
exercises.focus: One breath on Do over a drone in C
exercises.why: A long, steady note warms up your breath and your ear together.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Your pitch shows there as a line. Breathe in for four clicks. Sing {{1}} on "ah" for as long as feels easy. Watch your pitch line stay flat. Count the clicks you held it for: you will compare on day 7.

exercises.title: Steps or skips?
exercises.focus: Major 2nd vs major 3rd by ear
exercises.why: Hearing whether a melody steps or skips is the first thing your ear needs to sing it back.

sections.text: Press Start below and the game plays two notes: a step (M2, Do to Re) or a skip (M3, Do to Mi). Pick the one you heard. Press Replay to hear it again.

exercises.title: Do Mi Sol over the drone
exercises.focus: Do Mi Sol in C, up and back
exercises.why: Do, Mi and Sol are the notes of the home chord, so most tunes lean on them.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Sing {{1}} {{3}} {{5}}, then back down to {{1}}. Sing the names: they help you remember each sound. Hold each note until your line settles on it.

exercises.title: Two step tunes
exercises.focus: Easy Do Re Mi tunes in C
exercises.why: Short tunes turn the notes into music you remember.

sections.text: First tune
A tune on Do, Re and Mi. Press Play to hear it, then press Sing with the mic and sing along. Your pitch shows on the staff as you go.
Second tune
Another tune on the same three notes. Look at the staff first and guess how it goes. Sing your guess. Then press Play to check.

exercises.title: Hum and open
exercises.focus: Hum to "ah" on Do and Sol in D
exercises.why: Humming lets you find a pitch quietly before you sing it out.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Hum {{1}} until your line sits on the note. Then open the hum to "ah" and keep your line where it was. The "ah" takes the pitch you found into your full voice. Then try the same on {{5}}.

exercises.title: A skipping tune
exercises.focus: An easy Do Mi Sol tune in D
exercises.why: A tune that skips puts day 1's Do Mi Sol into a melody.

sections.text: Press Play to hear it, then press Sing with the mic and sing along. When it feels easy, look away from the staff and sing it from memory.

exercises.title: 3rd or 5th?
exercises.focus: Major 3rd vs perfect 5th by ear
exercises.why: Do to Mi and Do to Sol are the week's two skips, and telling them apart by ear makes them easier to sing.

sections.text: Press Start below and the game plays two notes: a major 3rd (M3, Do to Mi) or a perfect 5th (P5, Do to Sol). Sing them back. Then pick the one you heard.

exercises.title: Do and Sol over chords
exercises.focus: Do over D, Sol over A
exercises.why: Singing a chord's note while the chord sounds is how a voice fits into music.

sections.text: Start the mic on the staff, then press Play below to start the chords: D and A take turns, one bar each. Sing {{1}} (D) when the D chord comes round. Sing {{5}} (A) when the A chord comes round. Then try {{3}} (F♯) over D instead.

exercises.title: A long Do in G
exercises.focus: One breath on Do over a drone in G
exercises.why: Coming back to the long note every few days lets your breath grow without strain.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Breathe in for four clicks. Sing {{1}} on "ah" for as long as feels easy. Watch your pitch line stay flat. Stop before you run out of breath: the end of the note should be as steady as the start.

exercises.title: 5th or 6th?
exercises.focus: Perfect 5th vs major 6th by ear
exercises.why: La sits one step above Sol, so hearing the two apart prepares today's tune.

sections.text: Press Start below and the game plays two notes: a perfect 5th (P5, Do to Sol) or a major 6th (M6, Do to La). Pick the one you heard.

exercises.title: Sol La Sol
exercises.focus: An easy La tune in G
exercises.why: Sol La Sol is the lift at the top of many children's songs.

sections.text: Press Play to hear it, then press Sing with the mic and sing along. Find Sol La Sol on the staff: the line goes up a step and back.

exercises.title: Over G and D
exercises.focus: Do, Mi and Sol over I and V in G
exercises.why: Choosing which chord note to sing is the first step of making up a melody.

sections.text: Start the mic on the staff, then press Play below to start the chords. Sing {{1}} (G) or {{3}} (B) when the G chord comes round. Sing {{5}} (D) when the D chord comes round. Pick a different note each time round.

exercises.title: Siren to Sol
exercises.focus: Glide Do to Sol and back in F
exercises.why: A slow glide loosens the voice and shows on the staff where your pitch goes between notes.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Glide slowly from {{1}} up to {{5}} and back on "ng", the sound at the end of "sing": it keeps your voice light while it slides. Watch your line curve between the notes. Then sing the two notes on their own, without the glide.

exercises.title: A tune under Do
exercises.focus: An easy tune that dips below Do, in F
exercises.why: Many tunes dip under Do before they come home.

sections.text: Press Play to hear it, then press Sing with the mic and sing along. Watch your line on the staff dip under Do, then come back up to it.

exercises.title: Skips, falling
exercises.focus: Major 3rd and perfect 5th, falling
exercises.why: Skips come downward too, and they sound different falling.

sections.text: Press Start below. Day 2's skips, now falling. The game plays two notes: a major 3rd (M3, Mi down to Do) or a perfect 5th (P5, Sol down to Do). Pick the one you heard.

exercises.title: Over F, B♭ and C
exercises.focus: Chord notes over I-IV-V in F
exercises.why: Three chords give your voice three notes to find.

sections.text: Start the mic on the staff, then press Play below to start the chords. Sing {{1}} (F) when the F chord comes round. Sing {{4}} (B♭) when B♭ comes round. Sing {{5}} (C) when C comes round. Hold each note for the whole bar. Then try {{3}} (A) over F instead.

days.theme: Do Mi Sol in a new key

exercises.title: Long Sol
exercises.focus: Sol, then Do, held over a drone in A
exercises.why: Holding a note that is not Do tests your pitch against the drone.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Sing {{5}} on "ah" for as long as feels easy. Watch your line stay flat on the note. Then do the same on {{1}}.

exercises.title: Steps and skips, mixed
exercises.focus: Major 2nd, major 3rd, perfect 5th by ear
exercises.why: Mixing the week's intervals checks that your ear knows each one on its own.

sections.text: Press Start below and the game plays two notes: a major 2nd (M2), a major 3rd (M3) or a perfect 5th (P5). Pick the one you heard.

exercises.title: Do Mi Sol in A
exercises.focus: Do Mi Sol up, down and skipped, over a drone in A
exercises.why: A new key moves every note, but Do Mi Sol sounds the same.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Sing {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} up and back down. Then skip around: {{5}} {{1}} {{3}} {{1}}. Then make up your own order. Hold each note until your line settles on it.

exercises.title: A harder skipping tune
exercises.focus: A medium Do Mi Sol tune in A
exercises.why: A longer tune puts the skips inside phrases you have to remember.

sections.text: Learn it
Press Play and sing along softly. Then press Sing with the mic and sing it phrase by phrase.
Sing it through
Now sing the whole tune with the mic before you press Play. Then press Play to check.

exercises.title: Do Re Mi Re Do
exercises.focus: Steps over a drone in C
exercises.why: Most melodies move by step, so steps need to land as cleanly as skips.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Sing {{1}} {{2}} {{3}} {{2}} {{1}}. Sing the names: they help you remember each sound. Watch your line step up, then back down.

exercises.title: A medium step tune
exercises.focus: A medium Do Re Mi tune in C
exercises.why: A tune that starts away from Do trains you to hear where home is.

sections.text: Look at the staff first. Sing the tune the way you think it goes. Then press Play to check. Then press Sing with the mic and sing it.

exercises.title: Hear and sing back
exercises.focus: Major 3rd and perfect 5th, sung before answering
exercises.why: Singing an interval back before you name it ties your ear to your voice.

sections.text: Press Start below and the game plays two notes: a major 3rd (M3) or a perfect 5th (P5). Sing both notes back. Then pick the one you heard.

exercises.title: A tune in 3rds
exercises.focus: An easy tune climbing in 3rds, in C
exercises.why: Climbing in 3rds mixes steps and skips in one phrase, the way real melodies move.

sections.text: Press Play to hear it, then press Sing with the mic and sing along. Then sing it a little louder. Keep your line on the notes.

exercises.title: How long is your Do?
exercises.focus: One breath on Do over a drone in D, counted
exercises.why: Holding the long note again on the last day shows how your breath has grown.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the drone, then start the mic on the staff. Breathe in for four clicks. Sing {{1}} on "ah" for as long as feels easy. Watch your pitch line stay flat. Count the clicks you held it for. Compare with your count from day 1.

exercises.title: A Sol tune
exercises.focus: An easy tune down from Sol, in D
exercises.why: A new tune, sung first from the staff, shows how far your reading has come.

sections.text: Sing the tune from the staff before you hear it. Then press Play to check. Then press Sing with the mic and sing it.

exercises.title: The week's intervals
exercises.focus: Major 2nd, major 3rd, perfect 5th, major 6th
exercises.why: All four of the week's intervals together check your ear.

sections.text: Press Start below and the game plays two notes: a major 2nd (M2), a major 3rd (M3), a perfect 5th (P5) or a major 6th (M6). Pick the one you heard. The table under the game shows which ones you know best.

exercises.title: Your own line over chords
exercises.focus: Do Mi Sol over I-IV-V-I in D
exercises.why: Making up a line from notes you know is the reward for the week.

sections.text: Start the mic on the staff, then press Play below to start the chords. Make up a line from {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} (D, F♯, A), in any order. Lean on {{5}} when the A chord comes round: it is that chord's root. Record yourself on your phone. Listen back.
